content:
Northern Metropolis development is advancing rapidly, and most of the land in Kwu Tung, once a cluster of soy sauce factories and residential homes, has been levelled. Yuet Wo Soy Sauce Factory and Kui Lee Soy Sauce Factory still remain, but many homes have been bulldozed... A photojournalist compared aerial photographs from the beginning of this year and this month, showing that the land near the soy sauce factory has transformed from residential area into a stretch of sand and dirt.

Before the bulldozers arrived, some residents had packed up their belongings and moved away. Before leaving, they left a note on a wooden table saying they had relocated their ancestral tablets to a nearby ancestral hall. When departing their homes, people left behind photographs, defunct copies of «爽報», almanacs, farming straw hats, and other items. The district's Kam Yik tea house and the Da Doo Food Industries soy sauce plant have been razed, and the 70-year-old Church of the True Jesus has relocated to a new site.

Earlier this year, the buildings on the outer perimeter (top) of Yuet Wo Soy Sauce Factory were still standing.

In October this year, the land outside the soy sauce factory has become a construction site, with houses levelled.

Two-storey houses were gradually demolished from the beginning of this year and have now been razed to the ground.

This row of residential houses has now been torn down, with the site turned into a stretch of dirt.

Before the demolition, some residents had packed up their belongings and moved away. Before leaving, they left a note on a wooden table saying they had relocated their ancestral tablets to a nearby ancestral hall.
